blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Using Incoterms confidently means knowing not just what each one means, but when each one fits — and, more importantly, when it does not. EXW is fine between experienced partners, but painful with a first-time buyer who has no local agent. FOB is comfortable when both sides trust the port. CIF quietly transfers a lot of detail work to the seller, for a higher price.

In practice, the choice shapes how much work each side does, how much insurance matters, and who is left holding the problem if something goes wrong at a specific point in the journey.

The intermediate test is simple: can you explain, in one sentence, why you chose a particular Incoterm for a particular deal? If you can, you understand it. If you cannot, you are still guessing — and guessing is expensive.

items.q: According to the text, why is EXW painful with a first-time buyer who has no local agent?
options: Because the buyer must handle work they are not ready for
Because the seller refuses to arrange insurance
Because EXW is more expensive than the other terms
Because the port cannot be trusted
items.why: Inferência: EXV/EXW serve entre parceiros experientes; um comprador de primeira viagem, sem agente local, não tem estrutura para assumir tudo desde a porta da fábrica.

items.q: What does the text say CIF does?
options: It transfers a lot of detail work to the seller for a higher price
It puts all the risk on the buyer
It removes the need for insurance
It only works between experienced partners
items.why: "CIF quietly transfers a lot of detail work to the seller, for a higher price."

items.q: According to the text, the choice of Incoterm shapes all of these EXCEPT…
options: how much insurance matters
the market price of the goods themselves
how much work each side does
who is left holding the problem
items.why: O texto cita trabalho, seguro e quem fica com o problema — não o preço de mercado do produto.

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: You should be able to justify your choice in one sentence
Guessing the term can be costly
The best Incoterm is simply the cheapest one on paper
A good choice depends on the specific deal and the partner
items.why: Inferência: o texto argumenta que a escolha depende do contexto e do risco, não apenas do preço — CIF, por exemplo, custa mais mas pode ser a melhor escolha.

items.q: What does "and guessing is expensive" suggest about people who cannot explain their choice?
options: They should always choose EXW
They do not really understand the term and may pay for that mistake
They will pay a higher price for insurance
They need a local agent at every port
items.why: Inferência: quem não sabe justificar em uma frase ainda está adivinhando — e o erro sai caro.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Charlotte orientando a compradora antes da reunião com o gerente. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Okay, before you walk into that meeting, let's rehearse the one sentence you'll say to your manager. He won't ask for a lecture on Incoterms — he'll ask why you picked this one, and you need an answer that fits in a single breath.

So, for this deal you've gone with CIF. Good. Your reason is that the buyer is new, they have no agent at the destination port, and you'd rather the seller arranges the insurance and the freight than leave a first-timer holding the problem. Say exactly that. Short and clear.

Now, if he pushes back on the price, don't panic. Yes, CIF costs a little more. But if we used FOB instead, we would save on the quoted price and then spend three weeks sorting out shipping and cover ourselves — and we'd own the risk at the port. That trade-off isn't worth it here.

Whatever you agree, confirm it in writing afterwards. Never leave the term as a verbal handshake. One sentence in the room, one line in the email. Do that, and you'll sound like you've done this for years.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What does Charlotte want the buyer to prepare before the meeting?
options: A full lecture on every Incoterm
A list of alternative ports
One clear sentence explaining her choice
A written contract for the seller
items.why: "let's rehearse the one sentence you'll say to your manager… an answer that fits in a single breath."

items.q: Why did the buyer choose CIF for this deal?
options: Because the manager insisted on it
Because CIF is always the cheapest option
Because the seller refused to use FOB
Because the buyer is new and has no agent at the destination port
items.why: "the buyer is new, they have no agent at the destination port, and you'd rather the seller arranges the insurance and the freight."

items.q: According to Charlotte, what would happen if they used FOB instead?
options: The seller would arrange the insurance for free
The deal would fall through entirely
They would pay more but avoid all risk
They would save on price but handle shipping and own the risk at the port
items.why: "if we used FOB instead, we would save on the quoted price and then spend three weeks sorting out shipping… and we'd own the risk at the port."

items.q: What does Charlotte imply by saying the FOB "trade-off isn't worth it here"?
options: FOB is never a good term for any deal
The seller charges too much for FOB
The small saving is not worth the extra work and risk for this particular buyer
The manager will reject FOB no matter what
items.why: Inferência: ela reconhece a economia do FOB, mas para esse comprador iniciante o esforço e o risco extras superam o ganho.

items.q: How would you best describe Charlotte's advice at the end?
options: Say it clearly in the room, then confirm it in writing
A verbal agreement is enough between partners
Let the seller decide the term for you
Only worry about the term if a problem appears later
items.why: "One sentence in the room, one line in the email" — nunca deixar como aperto de mão verbal.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "CIF quietly transfers a lot of detail work to the seller." To transfer here means to…
options: cancel
move responsibility from one side to the other
explain in writing
reduce the cost of
items.why: Transfer = transferir: passar a responsabilidade de uma parte para a outra.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "With a first-time buyer, having a reliable ___ at the destination port makes EXW workable."
options: sentence
local agent
insurance
freight
items.why: Local agent = agente local, quem resolve as coisas no porto de destino.

items.q: "The choice shapes how much work each side does." To shape means to…
options: determine or influence the form of
delay
hide
pay for
items.why: Shape = moldar: definir ou influenciar como algo será.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Under CIF, the seller arranges the ___ so the goods are covered if they are damaged at sea."
options: port
sentence
insurance
agent
items.why: Insurance = seguro, que cobre os danos durante o transporte.

items.q: "If you cannot justify the term, you are still guessing." To guess means to…
options: trust your agent
confirm in writing
negotiate a lower price
decide without a clear reason
items.why: Guess = adivinhar: escolher sem uma razão clara — e, no texto, isso sai caro.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em negociações de comércio e logística. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The manager still has to sign off on the Incoterm before we quote." To sign off on means to…
options: mention casually
postpone
translate
formally approve
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "If the manager pushes back on the price, don't panic." To push back on means to…
options: forget about it
sign it quickly
agree immediately
resist or challenge it
items.why: Push back on = resistir, questionar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "We agreed the term but nobody followed through and put it in the contract." To follow through means to…
options: carry the action to completion
delegate to the seller
renegotiate the price
cancel the deal
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim aquilo que foi combinado.

items.q: "Switching to FOB won't move the needle much on the total cost." To move the needle means to…
options: take a long time
confuse the buyer
make a noticeable difference
cause a legal problem
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer uma diferença perceptível.

items.q: "Let's iron out who pays for insurance before we sign." To iron out means to…
options: print the contract
delay the shipment
resolve the remaining details or disagreements
increase the price
items.why: Iron out = acertar, resolver os detalhes ou desacordos que ainda restam.
